data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III (Creative Minds, Creative Schools) Latvia factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Latvia performed on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test. The creative thinking assessment includes 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Latvia’s mean creative thinking score is 35/60, significantly above the OECD average (33), and students’ relative performance is above expectations based on mathematics and reading performance. The note also reports proficiency distributions (92% at least Level 3; 26% at Level 5–6) and within-Latvia gaps by socio-economic status and gender, alongside associations between creative thinking and attitudes, school pedagogies, and digital activities. The document is descriptive and does not provide an explicit ML modeling approach, PV-combination method, or missing-data procedure in the excerpt.
